clause: Logic actions: set-variable + set-variable-mode + runtime expressions [STU-PRO-015,STU-PRO-016,STU-PRO-025]

scope.summary: Implement the logic actions writing/reading the shared StudioVariable primitives (MT-346/347) at runtime: set variable (writes a literal, alias, or expression result into a StudioVariable) and set variable mode (switches the active mode of a StudioVariableCollection for a target scope). Runtime expressions evaluate arithmetic on number variables, string concatenation, comparisons, and boolean logic, including reading mode-specific values. There is no separate prototype-only variable type. The set-variable/mode editor is an operator surface.
expected_tests: argus: set-variable + set-variable-mode editor reachable via author_ids
live: set-variable writes literal/alias/expression; set-variable-mode switches collection mode in scope; arithmetic/concat/compare/bool eval reads mode-specific values
acceptance_criteria_original: set-variable + set-variable-mode + runtime expressions over shared StudioVariable; author_ids + manual entry

spec_clauses.spec_clause_text: | Set variable | [STU-PRO-015] | writes a literal, alias, or expression result into a `StudioVariable` at runtime |
| Set variable mode | [STU-PRO-016] | switches the active mode of a `StudioVariableCollection` for a target scope |

[STU-PRO-025] Set-variable ([STU-PRO-015]) and conditional ([STU-PRO-026]) actions evaluate runtime expressions over `StudioVariable`s: arithmetic on number variables, string concatenation, comparisons, and boolean logic, including reading mode-specific values. The variable, collection, and mode primitives are exactly those in 14.10 ([STU-DS-022] through [STU-DS-028]); prototyping does not define a separate variable type.

[STU-DS-028] Number, string, and boolean variables participate in prototype runtime expressions and conditionals defined in 14.11 ([STU-PRO-025], [STU-PRO-026]); the variable primitive is shared between the design-system surface here and the prototyping surface there — there is no separate prototype-only variable type. ### 7. Styles versus Variables (StudioStyleRegistry) Styles capture reusable multi-property definitions (a full paint stack, a complete type spec, an effect stack, a grid) where variables capture single mode-aware values. The two are complementary: a style may consume variables, and both publish through libraries.

implementation_notes.naming: Vendor product names are provenance only. Studio ships Handshake-native names per [STU-SECTION-003].
implementation_notes.database: SurrealDB with the EventLedger is the only durable authority. SQLite, libSQL, Turso and PostgreSQL are forbidden, including in tests and dev caches.
implementation_notes.engine_split: GPU, WGSL and compute live in the studio-engine crate behind its traits. handshake_core must never gain a GPU dependency.
implementation_notes.routing: Navigation extends the existing address and bus seams. No new router.
implementation_notes.worktree: Code paths resolve against the WP-KERNEL-012 worktree, never main.

validator_focus: Confirm every acceptance row traces to a sentence in the cited spec clause carried in implementation_notes. A row with no spec basis is a fabrication.
Reject any row still carrying proof_target_status REQUIRED: it has no proof of its own.
Reject scaffold-only proof: at least one proof command must drive the executable runtime rather than a fixture the implementer authored.
Where the contract touches numeric parameters, confirm hard and soft bounds are stored as separate values and an unknown bound is stored as unknown, never mirrored.

resource_privacy_obligation.rule: Resources this contract reads, derives, caches or exports stay inside the authenticated operator's scope. No cross-identity read path may be introduced.
